36.0.0.en: Nebuchadnezzar deposed King Jehoiachin, and made his uncle Mattaniah king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah. He was twenty-one years old at that time, so as to show his authority over the kingdom, and he reigned about eleven years, like Jehoiakim his brother. Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim also each reigned about three months, and perhaps God allowed Jehoahaz to reign three months so that Jehoiakim, who came after him, would be careful and walk with God and not imitate his brother who preceded him, lest he be deposed; but unfortunately he did not obey God and worship Him. The same thing was repeated afterward, and Jehoiakim was concerned that his son Jehoiachin should reign, and he even made him king with him during his life for ten years, then he reigned after the death of Jehoiakim for three months, and after that Nebuchadnezzar carried him captive to Babylon. Zedekiah was not deterred and did not walk with God, so his end, after about eleven years, was that he too was carried captive to Babylon.

36.0.1.en: If only you would learn from the mistakes of others, so that you avoid them and return to God and keep His commandments, and so deliver yourself from the snares of the demons, and enjoy God's care and love.

36.1.0.en: Zedekiah's rule was marked by turning away from God, encouraging idol worship, and the spread of injustice and evil lusts. And more than this, they mistreated the prophets of God whom He sent, especially the great prophet Jeremiah, who was strong in proclaiming the truth to every class of the kingdom, in addition to other prophets, such as Daniel, Ezekiel, Baruch, and the prophet Urijah, who was killed in the days of Jehoiakim (Jer 26:20-23). We see the care of God, who in times of extreme weakness sends great prophets, such as Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel, to proclaim His voice with power.

36.2.0.en: Zedekiah was not content to walk in the way of evil, but also swore and pledged to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, that he would submit to him, but he rebelled against him again (Ezek 17:18). Despite all of Jeremiah's warnings and admonitions, he was stubborn and refused to return to God by repentance.

36.3.0.en: As for the chief priests, the teachers, the leaders and all the people, they were influenced by Zedekiah's evil, so they worshipped idols and defiled the house of the Lord by abandoning His Law and walking against it, and so they provoked God to anger.

36.4.0.en: God's tenderness toward His people appears in His warning them and calling them to repentance, a long time before the punishment came, which was the captivity. He sent His messengers the prophets, not only immediately before the captivity, such as Jeremiah, Daniel, Ezekiel and Urijah, mentioned before in (v. 12), but He also sent earlier Elijah, Elisha, Isaiah and other prophets, that perhaps they would repent and He would forgive them.

36.4.1.en: But they neglected the word of God, and even insolently mistreated His prophets, not only by mocking them but even by killing them, such as Isaiah, whom they sawed with a wooden saw. Consequently, since no remedy availed with them, and there was no longer an opportunity for them to be healed of their spiritual diseases, He was finally compelled to punish them with captivity, so that some of them might return to Him in repentance, and He would forgive them.

36.5.0.en: Since the people rejected God's tenderness and compassion toward them (v. 15), He allowed the king of Babylon to discipline them, so he besieged Jerusalem, then attacked it and killed those in it and had compassion on no one, whether young man or young woman, old or young. He was cruel and destroyed everyone he met, and this was in the year 587 BC. This is the natural result of evil: whoever neglects the longsuffering of God must in the end face troubles and destruction.

36.5.1.en: The opportunity of a lifetime is offered to you by God, so that you may know Him and repent of your sins. If only you would seize it, to draw near to Him and enjoy His care on earth, and then fellowship with Him and the sight of His glory, which cannot be expressed, in heaven.

36.6.0.en: Nebuchadnezzar also gathered what remained of the vessels of the house of the Lord, whether the large ones, such as the bronze pillars, or the small ones, such as the gold vessels used in the Holy Place; he took everything of value. Nebuchadnezzar had taken some of the vessels in the first captivity, in the days of Jehoiakim in the year 605 BC (v. 7), then another part, the precious one, in the days of Jehoiachin in the year 597 BC (v. 10), and now, in the year 587 BC, in the third captivity, at the end of Zedekiah's reign, he takes what remained in the house of the Lord. He also seized the chiefs responsible for the Temple and took possession of all the treasures that were in the house of the Lord and in the house of the king, and sent all this to Babylon.

36.7.0.en: After Nebuchadnezzar's army took everything precious in the house of the Lord, they burned it and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and they also burned the king's house and the palaces of the great men. Thus they destroyed Jerusalem in this third captivity. Four years after this, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, came to Jerusalem and took a number of captives to Babylon, and this is the fourth and last Babylonian captivity (Jer 52:30).

36.8.0.en: He refers here to those taken captive in the third and fourth captivities, who were sent to Babylon and became slaves to Nebuchadnezzar for seventy years, until Babylon fell and the kingdom of Media and Persia reigned in its place.

36.9.0.en: Thus the prophecy of the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled, that the Babylonian captivity would last seventy years, and this was the making up of the rest of the land, as the Law prescribed, for God commanded that they let the land rest in the seventh year and not sow it (Lev 25:4). But they neglected this for long periods, from the days of Joshua until the Babylonian captivity, and the period in which the land was neglected was about 490 years, during which they sowed the land in the seventh year, so that the number is 490 ÷ 7 = 70. Therefore God punished them by having the Chaldeans take possession of Jerusalem and Judah and destroy them, and cultivation in them was neglected, so the land rested by compulsion for seventy years, which is the length of the Babylonian captivity. God's people had also neglected everything connected with the seventh year, including the freeing of their brethren, the slaves whom they owned, so God allowed them all to be enslaved for seventy years, in repayment of the rights of their wronged brethren.
